_meta.note: balanceBullets: 3-5 bullets per spell. overridable[]: decisions the user can reasonably reverse. checklistFailures[]: 12-item checklist deviations requiring explicit acknowledgement.

_template:body-enhancement.summary: Partial-body morph spells (gestalt fiction) giving the caster a new natural attack or sensory modification. All are self-only, primal tradition only.
_template:body-enhancement.actionCost: 2 actions (standard combat-spell cost; 5e originals were 1 action or bonus action — boosted to 2 to match PF2e buff template)
_template:body-enhancement.duration: 1 minute for attack-granting entries (combat-grade); 1 hour for Sense (exploration-grade utility only)
_template:body-enhancement.defenseNotes: None (willing self-buff; morph not polymorph — partial body changes do not suppress other morphs)
_template:body-enhancement.scalingCadence: Qualitative step-ups at odd ranks (3rd/5th/7th/9th): damage die increases one step per two ranks, with a signature-flourish rider at 5th (crit or free action). Sense uses a linear unlock (1/2/3 senses at ranks 1/2/3).
_template:body-enhancement.anchor: Body Enhancement: Claws (already converted) — all siblings match its scaffold. Magic Fang (rank 1, primal, morph) is the published PF2e anchor for the series.
_template:body-enhancement.seriesRules: Fangs = piercing + grapple trait. Hide = temp HP + circumstance AC. Sense = sensory utility (not a strike). Horns = bludgeoning + shove + charge bonus (rank 2). Mind = Will save bonus + ability-score substitution (rank 2).

_template:monstrous-copy.summary: Higher-rank morph spells copying specific monster anatomy. All are self-only primal morph spells granting a powerful weapon or special ability derived from a named monster.
_template:monstrous-copy.actionCost: 2 actions for sustained-attack-grant entries (Tentacle, Claws, Tail, Stinger, Shell); 3 actions for multi-target ray entries (Eye Stalks); 2 actions for instantaneous AoE (Wail)
_template:monstrous-copy.duration: Sustained up to 1 minute for combat transforms (Tentacle, Claws, Tail, Stinger); 1 minute for Shell; instantaneous for Wail; varies for Eye Stalks (each ray duration is per its effect)
_template:monstrous-copy.range: self for transforms; 120 ft multi-target for Eye Stalks; 20-ft emanation for Wail
_template:monstrous-copy.traitList: concentrate, manipulate, morph, primal — plus spell-specific additions: poison for Tentacle/Stinger; auditory+mental+sonic+incapacitation for Wail; visual+incapacitation for Eye Stalks; earth for Claws
_template:monstrous-copy.defenseNotes: No save for transform entries (Tentacle, Claws, Tail, Stinger, Shell — they modify the caster). Save-based defense for offensive-use entries: Fortitude for Wail (body-impacting sonic) and Will for Eye Stalks rays.
_template:monstrous-copy.scalingCadence: Per-rank heightening on most entries (+1 damage die step per rank). Eye Stalks adds an additional ray at rank 8 and 9. Wail scales at +1/+2/+4 damage per tier per rank.
_template:monstrous-copy.anchor: Fiery Body (rank 7) — definitive self-buff polymorph benchmark. Slither (rank 5) — grapple-morph benchmark for Tentacle. Sunburst (rank 7) — AoE with incapacitation for Wail reference.
_template:monstrous-copy.seriesRules: Ranks 5–9 across the series. Each entry names its source monster explicitly in description. Incapacitation mandatory on Wail (unconsciousness on crit fail) and Eye Stalks (combat-removal rays). Poison affliction for Tentacle/Stinger uses multi-stage PF2e affliction format to avoid incapacitation gating at lower save tiers.

_template:shape-modify.summary: Modifier-on-top-of-transformation spells (rank 3). All require the caster to already be in wild shape or a polymorph effect. Each imposes a trade-off (gain X, lose Y). All are primal morph.
_template:shape-modify.actionCost: 1 action (these are modifier-spells layered onto an existing transformation, not initiating a new one; 5e used bonus action → PF2e 1 action is the canonical mapping)
_template:shape-modify.duration: Until the active wild shape ends (tied to the parent transformation)
_template:shape-modify.scalingCadence: Qualitative step-ups at ranks 5 and 7 (Heightened 5th/7th), progressively weakening the penalty side of the trade-off while amplifying the bonus side. No (+1) heightening — the 'until form ends' duration is already non-standard.
_template:shape-modify.anchor: Heroism (rank 3) — status-bonus benchmark. Haste (rank 3) — speed-grant benchmark. No published PF2e spell exactly mirrors the 'modifier-on-transformation' design; the series occupies a unique design niche.
_template:shape-modify.seriesRules: Four entries at rank 3: Accuracy (attack bonus / damage penalty), Armor (AC bonus / Speed penalty), Severity (damage bonus / attack penalty), Speed (Speed bonus / AC penalty). Accuracy and Severity are mirrors; Armor and Speed are mirrors. Each has a distinct material component matching the 5e original. Prerequisite 'must be in a polymorph or morph effect' is enforced as a cast condition.
_template:shape-modify.designDecision: 5e original coupled casting these with actually wild-shaping (expending a charge). PF2e has no wild shape charges — the series is redesigned as modifier-on-existing-transform. They cannot initiate a transformation.

Acupuncture.anchor: Acid Grip (rank 2) — spell attack roll, damage + rider on hit
balanceBullets: Anchored to rank-2 spell-attack damage (Moderate column level 3: ~2d8+5 avg 14); 4d6 (~14) is exactly at the moderate benchmark.
Heal suppression for 1 round is the spell's signature rider; this is a minor duration (only until next turn start) which justifies not reducing damage for it.

Resistance/vulnerability/immunity reveal is a divination rider — no direct combat damage equivalent, but useful battlefield information. Priced as worth roughly half a dice of base damage in narrative value.
Mental trait ensures mindless creatures (oozes, most undead, constructs) cannot be read via pressure points — appropriate immunities gate.
overridable: Heal suppression could be extended to 'until the start of the target's next turn' (one full round) vs 'until the start of your next turn' for more relevance in turn order.
The 'learn resistance/vulnerability/immunity' rider could be separated into a persistent slow-reveal (learn one per round while sustained) for greater tactical value.

Almonk's Arcane Drain.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Slow (rank 3, slowed 1 min on fail) or Feeblemind (rank 7, stupefied 4); Arcane Drain targets spell economy, not action economy
balanceBullets: No published PF2e spell drains spell slots. The effect is unique: it directly reduces the target's spellcasting resources rather than their actions or conditions. This is potent against spellcaster enemies but useless against non-casters.
Will save is the correct mapping: 'disrupting the spellcasting faculty' is a mental/willpower contest, not a physical one.
Base rank drains a slot of rank 4 or lower — at rank 3, the caster-level is 5, so draining a 4th-rank slot is targeting one rank above the spell itself, appropriate for a control spell.
Heightening by +1 rank-cap-per-rank is clean and canonical: no need to track the 5e 'cast at N → drain N-rank slot' formula.
Named-caster series (Almonk's Arcane Drain/Siphon/Retribution): the three share an anti-magic Weave antillurgy theme; this entry is the offensive member.
overridable: Named-caster (Almonk's): PF2e-idiomatic is a focus spell for an antillurgy specialist. Kept as regular spell per plan directive.

The 'useless against non-spellcasters' limitation could be addressed by adding a secondary effect on non-casters (e.g., stupefied 1 for 1 round) — but this would change the spell's tight niche design.
checklistFailures: Named-caster spell (Almonk's): PF2e-idiomatic conversion is a focus spell; kept as regular spell per plan directive.

Almonk's Arcane Siphon.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Counterspell (reaction, arcane/occult, negates a spell at the cost of expending a slot of equal or higher rank); Siphon negates AND recovers a slot at lower power
balanceBullets: Counterspell (standard) costs a slot of equal rank to the intercepted spell; Arcane Siphon costs a rank-3 slot but recovers one slot of (absorbed rank - 1). Net slot cost: if absorbing a rank-3 spell, net cost is 0 slots (spent 3, recovered 2). This is strong but gated by: (a) sustained up to 1 min, (b) only single-target spells, (c) only catches one spell total.

Sustained requirement (not 'free 1-minute duration') is the primary balance lever: the caster must spend 1 action per round to maintain the orb, which costs action economy in exchange for the anti-magic effect.
The 5e '1 minute, no concentration' was changed to sustained because a free spell-denial orb that requires zero maintenance is too powerful — the sustain cost is the balancing force.
Named-caster series companion to Arcane Drain: Drain is offensive (drain slots from enemy), Siphon is defensive (catch a spell, recover own slots).
The temporary Focus Point on rank-1 absorption is a minor reward for catching low-value spells and preserves the 'always gets something' design of the 5e spell.
overridable: Named-caster (Almonk's): PF2e-idiomatic is a focus spell. Kept as regular spell per plan directive.

The sustained requirement could revert to '1 minute, no sustain required' if the GM finds the action cost too punishing — this would make the spell comparable in power to a very strong defensive buff.
checklistFailures: Named-caster spell (Almonk's): PF2e-idiomatic conversion is a focus spell; kept as regular spell per plan directive.

The 'recover a spell slot' mechanic has no direct PF2e published equivalent — closest is the Focus Point system. Slot recovery was flagged as a design deviation from PF2e conventions; the spell may warrant GM review before deployment in a campaign.

Almonk's Retribution.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Wall of Fire (rank 4, sustained zone damage) for the sustained punishing-aura pattern; Almonk's Retribution targets spellcasting actions specifically, which is unique
balanceBullets: 6d6 fire damage per spell cast within the zone is strong but gated: only spellcasters take damage, only when they cast, and the spell still goes off (no counterspell effect); at rank 5 this is appropriately powerful for an anti-spellcasting zone
Basic Fortitude save (5e Con save → PF2e Fortitude) correct: fire damage to the body is a Fort effect

Sustained up to 1 minute (reduced from 5e's 10-minute concentration): 10-minute always-on anti-magic zone would trivially suppress all enemy spellcasting for an entire dungeon level; 1-minute cap brings it in line with combat-grade auras
+1d6 per +1 rank heightening follows the Wall of Fire template for sustained zone damage (+1 die/rank)
overridable: FOCUS SPELL SUGGESTION: Almonk's Retribution is strongly suited as a focus spell for an Almonk practitioner or anti-magic specialist; the named-caster association and narrow anti-spellcasting trigger make it ideal as a 1-focus-point sustained ability

GM may prefer the zone also triggers on magical abilities (activated items, class abilities with the concentrate trait) in addition to spell casting — this widens the trigger at the cost of more GM adjudication

Anomalous Object.anchor: no clean analog — temporal object duplication has no PF2e precedent; closest is Replicate (rank 5 alchemist) but that is a copy not a time-fetch
balanceBullets: The shared-state mechanic is the spell's signature: effects on one copy affect the other, preventing 'free unlimited use' of a charged item.
Object size limited to 1 Bulk prevents trivial duplication of Large weapons, full suits of armor, or powerful artifacts.
Sustained up to 1 hour is exploration-tier; the spell is unlikely to be sustained in combat (no combat effect from the duplicate object itself).
Spell attack roll required against attended objects provides meaningful resistance for the most valuable use case.
The 'if either is destroyed, both are destroyed' clause prevents using the duplicate as a disposable decoy for a precious item.
overridable: Object size could be reduced to 'light Bulk' to prevent duplication of shields, bows, etc. for combat advantage.
The attended-object attack roll could be replaced with a Thievery check to make the interaction more skill-based.
A rarity of uncommon would be appropriate given the potential for plot-bypass (duplicating a key, a letter, etc.).

Antimagic Shroud.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Fire Shield (rank 4 self-buff that retaliates against attackers) but that's 3 ranks higher
balanceBullets: No direct PF2e analog: a 'one-shot retributive anti-spell burst' is a unique design space. Fire Shield (rank 4) retaliates against melee attackers passively; this retaliates against spell casters but only once.

Damage reduced from 5e's 2d10 necrotic (avg 11) to 2d4 force (avg 5) to fit rank-1 retributive budget; the 10-minute passive protection duration is the primary value, the retributive burst is the trigger payoff.

Force type chosen over void because: (a) the 'compressed space decompresses' fiction matches kinetic/planar, (b) force is less resistable ensuring the retribution fires, (c) void at rank 1 would need divine/occult which misaligns with the Sorcerer/Warlock/Wizard source.
Basic Reflex save is appropriate for a sudden outward blast aimed at the caster.
overridable: Damage could be changed to void (necrotic) to match the 5e original; would require adding divine or occult tradition.
Could be redesigned as a reaction (1 action) instead of a pre-cast buff, making it a direct 'magic counterpunch' that grants the +2 bonus on the triggering save as well.
Could be raised to rank 2 with 2d8 force damage to feel more impactful as a 'shield' spell.

Arcane Censure.anchor: Dominate (rank 6, incapacitation, full mind control) — Arcane Censure is narrower (spellcasting only) but permanent on crit fail; rank 9 for permanence
balanceBullets: incapacitation MANDATORY: completely removing all spellcasting from an enemy spellcaster on a failed save is fight-removal for the most dangerous archetypes
1,000 gp diamond cost means one casting per major encounter at most; the permanent crit-fail tier is offset by the material cost barrier
Will save: spellcasting connection is a mental/essence bond — Will is the correct save for severing it
Daily save to end (on failure tier): 5e had no save recovery; giving 1-week-with-daily-saves on failure (only permanent on crit fail) creates a more graduated PF2e structure
overridable: Recovery method: 5e 'only Wish can undo' → PF2e 'rank-9 counteract attempt'; GM may restrict to only a rank-9 heal-equivalent or a specific ritual if they want to preserve the 5e severity
Affects innate magic: 5e included innate spellcasting; PF2e version matches — GM may narrow to 'prepared/spontaneous spell slots only' for a weaker version

Arcane Interdiction.anchor: Antimagic Field (rank 8, fully suppresses all magic in area) — Arcane Interdiction is a much weaker, rank-4 version that taxes rather than suppresses spellcasting
balanceBullets: The flat check mechanic (not a save) means the DC scales with the spell being cast, not with the target's saving throw modifier — this treats all casters equally regardless of Fortitude bonus.
DC 5 + spell rank means rank-1 spells have an 80% success rate (flat checks); rank-8 spells have a 35% success rate in the aura. This creates strategic tension without being an automatic shutdown.
The self-exemption for sustaining only (not for all spells the caster casts within the aura) is important: the caster still faces the check when casting other spells in their own aura.

Arcane only tradition is a deliberate narrowing — this spell manipulates the Weave (arcane flavor); divine/primal casters draw from different power sources and could be granted immunity or partial immunity at the GM's discretion.
overridable: The self-exemption could be broadened to 'all spells cast by the caster' rather than only the sustaining check, making the caster a free actor within their own aura.
Could be expanded to arcane + occult traditions if the Weave-manipulation flavor extends to occult metaphysics.
checklistFailures: Checklist item 12 — tradition list: arcane-only is a narrowing from the 5e Sorcerer/Warlock/Wizard list (which could imply occult via Warlock). Logged as deliberate design choice; overridable above.

Arcane Tattoo.anchor: Heroism (rank 3, +1 status bonus 10 min) — Arcane Tattoo stores Heroism-tier effects permanently until activated, which justifies rank 3
balanceBullets: The permanent-until-activated storage is the spell's power: it can be applied out of combat and activated as a 1-action during combat. This is stronger than a 2-action cast in the moment, justified by the 10-minute casting time and 15 gp material cost.

Each tattoo effect is roughly equivalent to one rank-3 buff: Red ≈ Haste partial; Yellow ≈ Bull's Strength; Green ≈ Haste (speed only); Purple ≈ Invisibility partial. None are full-rank-3 buffs — they're each a partial effect, appropriate for the pre-loaded design.
One-tattoo-at-a-time cap prevents stacking multiple stored buffs, keeping the spell from becoming a multi-buff economy exploit.
The 5e 200 gp material cost → 15 gp in PF2e (approximately 10× economy scaling): appropriate for a rank-3 utility with permanent storage.
Traditions arcane + occult: tattoos channel mental/material magic; primal and divine excluded as this is not nature or divine grace.
overridable: Could add divine and primal traditions if the GM wants tattoo magic to be accessible to more classes — thematically, runic tattoos exist in many cultural traditions including primal ones.

The 5e ritual flag could be preserved as 'this spell can only be cast as a 10-minute downtime activity' rather than a castable exploration spell — would add ritual gating without requiring PF2e's formal ritual system.

Artist's Rendition.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Wall of Stone (rank 5, permanent stone wall) but Artist's Rendition creates any mundane object, not just walls, at rank 3
balanceBullets: The 25 gp value cap and 'paste if higher-value' clause are the primary balance governors: this spell cannot create wealth, gems, or real weapons of significant value.
The 25 sq ft size limit restricts object scale to furniture-sized or smaller doors/pits; the spell cannot create fortifications or structures without extensive multi-casting.
Pit creation (10 ft deep) and doorway creation are the most tactically significant uses; both have explicit restrictions (1 ft stone / 3 ft wood) that limit their structural impact.
Energy creation (1d8 damage then gone) is a weak cantrip-level damage option; at rank 3, 1d8 is minimal and the dissipation means it's not a sustained damage source.
Permanent non-magical result is the spell's unique value: the created object outlasts the spell, unlike illusion duplicates.
overridable: The 25 gp value cap could increase with GM approval for specific in-fiction uses (e.g., creating a real weapon for an ally who is disarmed — this is a dramatic moment, not a wealth exploit).
The energy-type creation damage (1d8) could scale with heightening — currently it doesn't, which makes it largely irrelevant at rank 3+.

Ashen Pack.anchor: Flaming Sphere (rank 2, 3d6 fire basic Reflex sustained) — Ashen Pack is 3x Flaming Sphere equivalent at rank 4, with spell attack instead of basic Reflex and a knockdown rider
balanceBullets: 4d6 fire (14 avg) per wolf hit via spell attack roll vs rank-4 spell attack moderate budget (~12-14 avg at level 7) — within 1 row of table.
Three charges across the spell's 1-minute duration provide meaningful sustained damage potential; wolves are fragile and can be destroyed, creating resource management.
Knockdown (prone) on crit hit is appropriate: crit-only riders are free per the design checklist.
5e's double-dip (attack roll AND strength save vs prone) was collapsed to attack-roll-only with prone on crit — this is the correct PF2e idiom for attack-plus-condition effects.
overridable: Could restore the Fortitude save vs prone on any hit (not just crit) if the GM wants more reliable crowd control, but would require reducing damage to ~3d6 to compensate.
Wolf AC (= spell DC) is unusual in PF2e — could simplify to a fixed value (e.g., AC 20 at rank 4, scaling +2 per rank heightened).
checklistFailures: Checklist item 3 — action cost: 5e allowed sending a wolf as 'an action on each of your turns'; PF2e normalizes to 1 wolf per Sustain action. This halves the throughput from 5e's potential 3 wolves per round to 1 per round, which is necessary to fit PF2e's Sustain economy.

Attraction.anchor: Hydraulic Push (rank 1) — ST attack+knockback; adapted to AoE pull with Fortitude save
Attraction.archetype: area-damage-save (AoE bludgeoning + forced pull toward caster)
balanceBullets: Anchored to rank-1 area-damage template: 2d6 bludgeoning matches the rank-1 limited-use area table (2d6 avg 7).
Fortitude save chosen over Reflex because gravitational pull is bodily resistance (Con/Fort), not agility-based dodging.
The pull rider (10 ft on fail, 20 ft on crit fail) is priced into the save tiers rather than applying across all degrees — keeps the damage at the table-appropriate 2d6 baseline.
15-ft emanation is the canonical rank-1 emanation size; self-centered means the caster is the focal point which fits the gravity fiction.
overridable: Could change to a basic Reflex save (Fireball-style) with the pull reduced to crit-fail only, which is more standard for AoE area damage.
Could increase base damage to 2d8 if the pull is removed entirely (pure damage, no rider).

Awkward.anchor: Slow (rank 3, Fortitude, slowed 1 for 1 min on fail) — Awkward is similar in tier (debuff-without-damage, Will save, sustained 1 min) at rank 4 with a narrower but socially impactful penalty
balanceBullets: –1 status penalty on fail is intentionally mild: it affects attack rolls and Cha checks/saves, not all d20 rolls. The inability to benefit from fortune effects on those rolls is the distinguishing feature.
The 'unaware of the problem' clause is the spell's flavor-mechanical hook: targets cannot voluntarily avoid triggering it because they don't know it's happening.
Emotion + mental traits correctly gate this against creatures immune to emotional manipulation.
Critical failure upgrades to –2 and adds Dex saves — appropriate escalation for a rank-4 spell.
overridable: The 'cannot benefit from fortune effects' clause could be simplified to just the status penalty if the fortune-blocking feels too complex or punishing when combined with other party effects.
Could target Charisma checks only (not attack rolls) for a purely social-debuff version, reducing the combat impact.

Bending Bolt.anchor: Lightning Bolt (rank 3, 4d12 electricity basic Reflex, 120-ft line) — Bending Bolt is rank 4, same line shape, higher damage (8d6 vs 4d12≈26 vs 8d6=28), with the bend-point signature ability
balanceBullets: 8d6 electricity (28 avg) at rank 4 is 2 rows above Lightning Bolt's 4d12 (26 avg) at rank 3. The +2d6 expected from heightening LB to rank 4 (giving 5d12≈32) exceeds 8d6; so Bending Bolt actually deals slightly less damage than a heightened Lightning Bolt, balanced by the bend utility.
The bend-point ability is the signature feature: it allows targeting creatures behind cover or around corners, which is significant but requires planning.
Electricity damage at standard 1.0x pricing — no premium or discount.
Heightening adds both bends and damage (+2d6 per rank), which is the canonical area-damage heightening rate.
overridable: Damage could be reduced to 6d6 (matching the expected rank-4 line budget more conservatively) if the bend utility is considered a full power upgrade rather than a minor one.
The number of base bends could start at 2 (with heightening adding more) if the single bend at rank 4 feels insufficient for the spell's identity.

Bestial Rage.anchor: Haste (rank 3) — +1 action, 1 min, single target; Bestial Rage is narrower (wild shape only) but provides attack/damage boost rather than action
balanceBullets: The cast-simultaneously-with-wild-shape requirement is the primary balance restriction: this spell only functions as part of wild shaping, preventing it from being used outside that context.

+1 status to melee attacks and one die-step damage increase for 1 minute matches a moderate rank-3 buff; the dual disadvantage (attackers +1 circumstance) is the cost, matching the 5e 'advantage both ways' tradeoff.
Morph (not polymorph) is the correct trait: this layers on top of a wild shape without suppressing it, which is the intended design.
Primal-only tradition is correct: this is druid/gestalt animal magic, not arcane or occult.
The 'both sides benefit from the aggression' design creates a high-risk/high-reward dynamic appropriate for a battle-focused buff at rank 3.
overridable: Could be restricted to Druid or classes with Wild Shape class feat, rather than any primal caster — this would make it more like the intended focus-spell design.
The +1 circumstance to attackers could be framed as a –1 status to AC instead (equivalent mechanically, simpler to track).
checklistFailures: The 5e spell requires expending a Wild Shape charge as part of casting. PF2e does not have a Wild Shape charge system — Wild Shape is a class feat, not a per-day ability. The requirement was softened to 'must be cast simultaneously with a wild shape polymorph spell.' This is a design departure that should be flagged for GM review.

Blades of Bone.anchor: no clean analog for grapple-enhancing morph spell; closest is Enlarge (rank 2, size increase) or Animal Form (rank 5, battle form) but Blades of Bone is a morph, not a battle form — it adds damage to grapple actions rather than replacing attacks
balanceBullets: 3d6 piercing on Grapple initiation + 2d6 per turn grabbed: combined expected value over 2 rounds is 3d6 + 2×2d6 = 7d6 ≈ 24.5, below the rank-5 single-target save damage benchmark of 10d6 ≈ 35; appropriate for a damage source that requires Athletics checks (no save for the damage once grabbed)
The morph suppresses wildshape (Druid's signature ability) — meaningful trade-off that 5e also enforced; not incapacitating for the caster since they still have weapon attacks and spells
Sustained up to 1 minute (reduced from 5e's 10-minute concentration): combat morph cap per plan
Attacker-damage-return (1d6 piercing when hit by unarmed/natural attack) is a design addition; this is below the 'reactions dealing full-spell damage' anti-pattern since 1d6 is symbolic, not tactical
overridable: FOCUS SPELL SUGGESTION: Blades of Bone is well-suited as a focus spell for a gestalt-Druid or wild-grappler archetype; the self-only morph with a specific trigger (grapple) is a class-defining ability pattern
The attacker-takes-damage clause is a design addition not in the 5e text; GM may remove it if the spell already feels powerful enough with just the grapple bonuses

Blithering Gibberish.anchor: Slow (rank 3) — single-target Will save, sustained debuff with end-of-turn save; scaled down to rank 2 with speech/spellcasting suppression
balanceBullets: Anchored to Slow (rank 3) for the structural pattern: single target, Will save, sustained up to 1 min, end-of-turn saves. This is a weaker version at rank 2 because it does not affect all actions (only speech/verbal casting).
Incapacitation required: for caster enemies, suppressing all verbal/linguistic spellcasting is a combat-removal effect. Without incapacitation, this trivializes all BBEG casters at rank 2.
Stupefied 1/2 added as a concrete mechanically-expressed condition for 'can't think clearly enough to speak coherently' — this is the appropriate PF2e implementation of 'incoherent speech'.
Heightening (4th) to 3 targets and (6th) to 6 targets follows the published mass-debuff scaling curve (Fear 1→5 targets at rank 1→3; this is a weaker debuff so 1→3→6 at 2→4→6 is appropriate).
overridable: Incapacitation could be dropped if the suppression is narrowed to only linguistic spells (requiring the linguistic trait) rather than all verbal/concentrate spells — that would make it not a full incapacitation.
The stupefied condition could be dropped entirely, leaving only the speech/casting suppression as a non-condition effect.

Body Enhancement: Claws.anchor: Magic Fang (rank 1, primal, morph) — extends unarmed Strike damage
balanceBullets: Anchored to Magic Fang (rank 1): grants/upgrades a natural attack on a single morph-trait spell.
Damage at rank 1 starts at 1d6 vs 5e's 2d6 — 2d6 unarmed at level 1 outscales martial weapons and isn't supported by the Animal Form template or Magic Fang's published numbers.
Step-ups at 3rd/5th/7th/9th track the natural-attack scaling published in martial-style focus spells and reach 3d8 deadly-d10 at rank 9.
Bleed-on-crit rider at rank 5 is the 'claws-specific' flourish to differentiate this entry from generic Magic Fang.
Morph (not polymorph) is deliberate — this is a partial body change and shouldn't suppress other morphs the way full polymorphs do.
overridable: Could be redesigned as a 1-action focus spell tied to a druid/seeker/gestalt class feat — that's the more PF2e-idiomatic shape and is flagged in the plan's 'class-locked spell' risk note.
Starting damage could be 1d8 if you want it on par with a longsword at level 1 — adjust subsequent ranks accordingly.
Body Enhancement: Claws.seriesTemplateNote: This entry is the canonical Body Enhancement template. Fangs (piercing), Hide (defensive — temp HP / AC), Horns (charge bonus), Mind (mental save / Int), and Sense (Perception / low-light) will reuse this scaffold with the appropriate damage type / defense / ability swapped, and will reference this template explicitly to avoid drift.

Body Enhancement: Fangs.anchor: Magic Fang (rank 1, primal, morph); Body Enhancement: Claws (sample template)
balanceBullets: Follows the Body Enhancement: Claws template exactly: 1d6 piercing at rank 1, step-ups at 3rd/5th/7th/9th, reaching 3d8 deadly-d10 at rank 9.
The fangs-specific flourish is the grapple weapon trait (hold in jaws) and a free-Grapple on crit at 5th — mirrors the bleed-on-crit at 5th from Claws.
5e's instant-attack 3d6 + prone-save was far above a rank-1 budget (avg ~10.5 damage + control); converting to a sustained 1d6 buff is the correct PF2e calibration.
Morph (not polymorph) is deliberate — partial jaw modification shouldn't suppress other transforms.
Primal-only tradition matches Magic Fang's published tradition list and the matter+life essence pairing for body-shape spells.
overridable: The grapple weapon trait could be replaced with finesse if the design intent is more 'rapier-like fang' than 'hold prey in jaws' — both are defensible.
Free-Grapple on crit at 5th could be instead 1d4 persistent bleed (matching Claws at 5th exactly) if series uniformity is preferred over a distinctive flourish.
Body Enhancement: Fangs.seriesTemplateNote: Follows BE template. Fangs-specific: piercing damage, grapple weapon trait.

Body Enhancement: Hide.anchor: Mystic Armor (rank 1, item bonus to AC); Fiery Body (rank 7, self-transform temp HP) — scaled down to rank 1
balanceBullets: 5e gave a flat 'base AC 13+Con' buff for 8 hours without concentration — equivalent to always-on Heavy Armor but better at rank 1, which is clearly broken for PF2e.
Converted to 5 temp HP + +1 circumstance AC for 1 minute: temp HP is the primary resource (absorbed damage ends both benefits), making the spell inherently self-limiting.
Temp HP values (5/10/15/25/35 at ranks 1/3/5/7/9) match the healing-buffs-summons.md temp-HP table (~5×rank).
The +1 circumstance AC steps to +2 at rank 5 and +3 at rank 9, matching the Mystic Armor item-bonus progression as a rough parallel (different bonus type, so they stack).
Combat-grade buff cap (1 min) strictly enforced; the 5e 8-hour duration would be gamebreaking.
overridable: Could keep the 1-minute duration but drop the temp-HP linkage (AC bonus persists for the full minute independently). Simpler bookkeeping, slightly stronger.
Could use a flat resistance value instead of temp HP if the design goal is 'tougher skin' rather than 'absorb hits until breached'.
Body Enhancement: Hide.seriesTemplateNote: Follows BE template. Hide-specific: defensive (no attack), temp HP + circumstance AC, not an attack grant.

Body Enhancement: Horns.anchor: Body Enhancement: Claws (rank 1 template); Hydraulic Push (rank 1, spell-attack with push rider) — Horns is the rank-2 step-up for push/charge
Body Enhancement: Horns.archetype: buff (morph; natural attack grant with charge bonus)
balanceBullets: Rank bumped to 2 (from 5e level 1): 3d12 bludgeoning (avg 19.5) at level 1 is far above the rank-1 budget (max ~7 avg for a slotted 1-target spell); rank 2 with 1d8 and a charge rider is the correct calibration.
Charge bonus (fatal d12 + free Shove after 20 ft Stride) is the horns-specific flourish. Fatal d12 on a 1d8 base brings the crit ceiling to 1d12 minimum, rewarding the setup.
Three simultaneous 5e charge options (push, prone, or +1d12) collapsed to one (shove + fatal) to avoid the 'Everything Spell' anti-pattern.
Bludgeoning at 1d8 base (larger die than Claws/Fangs at 1d6 piercing) is appropriate for a heavier-impact natural weapon at the rank-2 tier.
Morph (not polymorph) — partial horn growth, same rationale as other BE entries.
overridable: Knock-prone on charge could be restored as a Fortitude save on hit if you want the traditional 'goring charge' flavor — would require a save action and slightly more complexity.
The fatal d12 could be replaced with a +1d12 damage bonus on charge, closer to the original +1d12 option in the 5e text.
Body Enhancement: Horns.seriesTemplateNote: Follows BE template at rank 2. Horns-specific: bludgeoning, shove weapon trait, charge bonus with fatal d12.

Body Enhancement: Mind.anchor: Heroism (rank 3, +1 status to attacks/saves/skills/Perception, 10 min) — Mind is below Heroism in breadth and duration (1 min, Will saves + limited ability-swap only).
Body Enhancement: Mind.archetype: buff (morph; cognitive enhancement, Will save bonus)
balanceBullets: 5e's 'use Wisdom in place of any ability score' is extremely broad; converted to three discrete options to avoid an 'everything' buff at rank 2.
+2 status to Will saves at rank 2 is calibrated against Heroism's +1 to all at rank 3 (shorter duration, narrower scope = one step earlier is acceptable).
1-minute duration enforced (5e was 1-minute concentration). Heroism at 10 minutes justifies its rank-3 placement; Mind at 1 minute with narrower scope is rank 2.

Heightening unlocks additional ability-swap options rather than increasing the bonus — at rank 4 you can choose 2, at rank 6 you gain all three, matching the Sense heightening philosophy of 'unlock more options'.
No attack modifier, no damage modifier — this is a pure mental-defense/utility entry in the BE series.
overridable: The Will-save bonus could be dropped entirely and replaced with a pure ability-substitution mechanic if you want the spell to feel more like 'cognitive flexibility' than 'mental fortitude'.
Heightened (9th) bonus increase (+1 to all bonuses) could be removed for simplicity; rank-9 players typically have better buff options available.
Body Enhancement: Mind.seriesTemplateNote: Follows BE template at rank 2. Mind-specific: Will save status bonus + ability-score substitution options. No attack grant.

Body Enhancement: Sense.anchor: No direct PF2e published analog for a sensory-morph spell; closest is Darkvision (rank 2) and See the Unseen (rank 2). Sense is purposely below rank 2 because it grants only partial sensory upgrades (not full darkvision).
balanceBullets: Exploration-grade spell: 1-hour duration is correct because Sense is purely utility, not combat-capable.
Low-light vision for sight is weaker than darkvision (rank 2) — appropriate at rank 1; designed to not eclipse the rank-2 sensory slot.
+2 circumstance to Perception (hearing) and Survival/Track (scent) are meaningful exploration bonuses without combat impact.
Heightening unlocks 2-then-all senses matching the 5e text exactly — the 5e design was already well-calibrated for a sense-utility spell.
No damage, no save, no combat utility — this is the purest utility entry in the BE series and is costed accordingly.
overridable: The sight option could grant darkvision instead of low-light vision if you want the rank-1 slot to feel more impactful; would then compete more directly with rank-2 Darkvision.
Could be redesigned as a 1-hour ritual (no slot) given its purely exploratory nature — closer to how PF2e handles long-duration sensory effects.
checklistFailures: Checklist item 3 (action cost matches power): 5e was bonus action; PF2e is 2 actions. A 1-action cast would be permissible for a utility-only spell with 1-hour duration — 2 actions is conservative. Flagged but not changed (the BE template standardizes to 2 actions for series consistency).
Body Enhancement: Sense.seriesTemplateNote: Follows BE template except: 1-hour exploration duration instead of 1-minute combat duration. No attack grant. Heightened (Xth) style instead of (odd-rank) style.

Bodydouble.anchor: Mirror Image (rank 2, illusion, self, 1 min — 3 images intercept attacks); Bodydouble is rank 3 and adds offensive projection rather than defensive intercept
balanceBullets: Mirror Image (rank 2) is purely defensive; Bodydouble (rank 3) is primarily offensive — using the double as an attack origin point rather than an attack-intercept screen. This is the correct rank-step difference.
The double cannot be attacked or interacted with, which means it has no defensive value at all — unlike Mirror Image — preserving the offensive-only niche.
Sustained up to 1 min (PF2e combat cap) with a Sustain-to-reposition design means the double's position must be actively maintained, preventing free persistent range extension.
Perception-check disbelieve (DC = spell DC) gives counterplay without trivializing the double; creatures that witness the effect can attempt to understand it.
Traditions arcane + divine + occult (kosmoturgy/space-bending spans matter+mind / spirit+life / mind+spirit); primal excluded.
overridable: Could add the teleportation trait if the GM interprets the double's projection as a spatial shift for the caster rather than a separate constructed image — this would make Dimensional Lock affect the spell.

The double could be given a defensive function (counts as cover for the caster) at the base rank — currently it's purely offensive, which may disappoint players who want the defensive Mirror-Image feel.

Bound Minds.anchor: Telepathic Bond (rank 5, arcane) — multiple creatures share mental communication
balanceBullets: Telepathic Bond at rank 5 creates communication links between up to 5 willing creatures for 1 hour. Bound Minds at rank 7 creates a deeper link (location + condition + emotion, no communication) between exactly 2 creatures for 1 year — the qualitative depth and duration justify the 2-rank increase.
The link conveys only state, not surroundings — this is intentionally restricted to prevent it from functioning as a permanent remote sensing / Scrying.
1-year duration is appropriate for a rank-7 ritual-tier buff (1-hour cast time); this is a 'bond for a campaign arc' spell.
No combat value whatsoever — purely social and exploration utility.
Permanent at rank 9 is the appropriate qualitative unlock for a 2-rank heightening (per heightening rules: duration tier up ≈ +2 ranks).
overridable: Duration at base could be '1 year' but with a clause that it is disrupted by Detect Magic / Dispel Magic of rank 7+ to prevent it from being truly permanent before rank 9.
Could add uncommon rarity — a permanent mental link has significant social and setting implications.

Bubble Bubble.anchor: Grease (rank 1, Reflex, -10 ft Speed + prone on crit fail) — Bubble Bubble is a rank-4 version with a more persistent and multi-faceted debuff (clumsy + speed + spellcasting restriction)
balanceBullets: The goop condition (clumsy 1 + –10 ft Speed + no manipulate spells) is meaningful but not incapacitating — does not require the incapacitation trait.
The 'action to remove' clause (Acrobatics/Athletics vs spell DC) creates a meaningful decision for affected creatures: spend an action to clear the condition or fight through the penalty.
Reflex save (Dex organ mapping from 5e Dex save) is correct — dodging a splash effect.
Heightening adds bubbles (targets) rather than damage, matching the Force Barrage / auto-hit pattern.
overridable: The 'cannot cast manipulate-trait spells' clause could be changed to a flat check (DC 8) to cast manipulate spells, giving casters a chance to push through rather than being hard-blocked.
Clumsy 1 could be replaced with off-guard (weaker, affects only AC) to reduce the overall debuff package if the combination of effects feels too strong.

Carnage.anchor: Desiccate (rank 8, 10d10 AoE Fortitude) — rank-8 damage budget; Carnage is single-strike AoE with teleport, so calibrated lower per-hit
balanceBullets: 6d6 force (~21 avg) bonus on the initial burst vs. all adjacent creatures; force at 0.80× pricing means effective budget is ~7.5d6 equivalent — appropriate given the caster also delivers a full weapon Strike simultaneously
Sustained follow-up at 4d6 force per turn is weaker (sustain = 1 action, not 2) — matches the design rule that sustained effects are ~80% of initial cast value

Incapacitation on stunned-1 crit fail: required because stunned removes turns. At rank 8 vs most bosses (level 16+) the incapacitation gate applies (level > rank 8 × 2 = 16), meaning level 17+ creatures save one step better
Teleportation trait means anti-teleport effects (Dimensional Lock) suppress the movement component, which is a meaningful tactical counterplay
5e Carnage entries for 2nd/3rd/4th use were empty in source data — the sustained Continued Carnage action was designed from the effect budget, not literal 5e text; flagged as GM decision point
overridable: Continued Carnage teleport distance: set at 60 ft for follow-up (vs 120 ft on cast); GM may allow full 120 ft each turn if they want a more mobile caster
Stun on crit fail: currently stunned 1; GM may upgrade to stunned 2 for a more dramatic high-end result
checklistFailures: 5e source entries for 2nd/3rd/4th Carnage use were empty JSON arrays — the follow-up action was designed autonomously from budget; if the author had specific effects in mind they would need to be retrofitted

Celestial Preservation.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Gentle Repose (rank 2, preserves a body from decay) plus aspects of Raise Dead logistics. Celestial Preservation dramatically exceeds Gentle Repose in narrative scope (constellation, planar permanence) at rank 4.
balanceBullets: This spell solves a logistics problem (resurrection deadline) rather than granting combat power; its rank-4 cost is justified by the narrative scale (turning a body into a visible constellation) and the permanent until-raised duration.
Night-only restriction and material cost (25 gp) provide meaningful constraints for a permanent-duration utility.
Heightening at 6th and 8th ranks extends the death-duration threshold rather than adding power — appropriate for a qualitative unlock pattern.
Rare rarity applied: this spell creates a semi-permanent sky feature and has major in-world narrative consequences (anyone with Astronomy can see the new star).
overridable: Could be redesigned as a ritual (multiple casters, 1-day cast, higher material cost) for stronger thematic weight.
The 'visible constellation' could be kept private (only visible to those with the Detect Magic spell or similar) to reduce the setting-impact.

Cerebral Disruption.anchor: Touch of Madness (rank 8, permanent mental curse) — Cerebral Disruption is the touch-range rank-9 version with a d6 table of distinct psychological effects
balanceBullets: Touch range + rank 9 slot cost are the primary balance levers for a spell that imposes permanent stupefied 4 and a persistent curse on a failed save

9d6 mental damage (~31 avg) on failure is below typical rank-9 save damage (~80 for a pure damage spell) — justified because stupefied 4 permanent is an enormous condition rider (per checklist: subtract ~2 rows for major conditions; rank 9 damage budget is significantly consumed by the curse)
incapacitation MANDATORY: permanent stupefied 4 + confused periodic + amnesia are all Tier S or Tier A incapacitation-level effects
d6 curse table preserves the 5e variety while staying in the PF2e design language; each effect is meaningful but no single result trivializes the encounter on its own
overridable: Confusion in failure table: 5e Confusion was ongoing until removed; PF2e version gives the daily-save Confusion trigger instead of permanent Confusion (permanent Confusion without save would be too strong even at rank 9); GM may make it permanent-Confusion to match 5e fully
Save type for the curse table effects: GM may add additional individual Will saves for each curse trigger if they want a finer-grained mechanic

Charming.anchor: Charm (rank 1, single target; incapacitation at rank 2) — Charming is the mass variant; all visible creatures within 30 feet makes this a rank-5 spell per the mass-charm scaling (Charm 1→rank 5 for mass is a larger jump than the Confusion 4→8 for mass pattern, but Charming is not as total-control as Dominate)
balanceBullets: Incapacitation trait is mandatory: charmed creatures will not attack the caster, which effectively removes them from the combat encounter on a failed Will save — this meets the incapacitation threshold

Base duration reduced from 12 hours (5e) to 1 hour: 12-hour mass charm at rank 5 would allow charming an entire dungeon population before entering; 1 hour still enables significant exploration/social use while preventing trivial encounter bypass
Will save (5e Wisdom save → PF2e Will) correct: charm is a mental/emotion effect targeting the mind

+2 circumstance bonus to save if combat is ongoing (5e 'advantage if fighting' → PF2e +2 circumstance bonus): prevents Charming from being an auto-win mid-combat tool; enemies get a meaningful bonus when their blood is up
overridable: Duration: 1 hour at base vs 12 hours in 5e is a significant reduction; GM may prefer 8 hours if the table uses Charming primarily for social/exploration scenarios rather than combat bypass
Fascinated 1 round on failure is a design addition (transition state); GM may prefer direct charm without the fascinated bridge if the transition feels mechanically fiddly
Heightened 7th = 24 hours, 9th = 1 week: the 5e spell had a flat 12-hour duration with no heightening for duration; these tiers are design additions to give the spell meaningful heightening

Charming Memory.anchor: Charm (rank 1) — social enchantment with 1-hour exploration duration
balanceBullets: Anchored to Charm at rank 1: both are social enchantments with 1-hour duration.

5e's '+1d4 to any Charisma check or saving throw' (avg +2.5 to everything) is above rank 1 budget — Heroism at rank 3 gives +1 status to everything including saves; a rank-1 spell with +1d4 avg 2.5 to Cha saves eclipses that.
Reduced to +1 status on Deception/Diplomacy/Performance only (social skills) to stay comfortably within rank 1 bounds.
Heightening follows the Heroism status-bonus curve: +1 at rank 1, +2 at rank 4, +3 at rank 7.
overridable: Could include Intimidation in the base effect at rank 1 (all four social skills), at the cost of being slightly above the Charm anchor.
Could be redesigned to target others rather than self (plant memories in one willing creature; that creature gains the social bonus when interacting with you) for stronger 5e fidelity.

Checkpoint.anchor: no clean analog — designed from rank-9 healing budget (Heal rank 9 = 9d8+72 HP average 112); no published PF2e spell provides preemptive revival on a standard slot
balanceBullets: 1,000 gp Lasinium shard cost (consumed) is a hard gating mechanism — at rank 9 this is expensive but not prohibitive for high-tier play

Single-activation: the checkpoint fires once then ends; cannot be maintained indefinitely on one creature; the 1-hour duration window and single-fire constraint prevent it from being an always-on immortality effect

Healing amount anchored to rank-9 Heal (9d8+72 ≈ 112 HP): restores significant HP but not necessarily full HP at high levels (a level 17+ caster may have 200+ HP); rank 10 heightened restores full HP as the upgrade
Temporal/chronomancy flavor justified: this is a time-crystal anchor that 'saves' a moment in time, not direct healing — the healing activation is the mechanical consequence of a temporal effect
overridable: Activation condition: '0 HP or would die outright' — GM may include 'reduced to dying 3' as a trigger if they want the checkpoint to fire slightly earlier
Healing amount: fixed at 9d8+72 (rank-9 Heal) — GM may change to 'restore target to full HP' if they prefer simpler resolution and accept the stronger outcome
checklistFailures: No clean analog: no published PF2e spell provides on-death preemptive revival via a standard spell slot. The spell was designed entirely from budget. Flagged 'no clean analog'.

Chrysalis.anchor: no clean analog — PF2e has no rest-compression spell; Chrysalis is a unique exploration-utility spell at rank 6
balanceBullets: Rank 6 slot + 500 gp material component to give 1 ally a long rest in 1 hour: the recipient gains ~full HP recovery and ability refresh; powerful but strictly exploration-tier (cannot be used in combat)
The cocoon's AC 10, Hardness 5, 20 HP is fragile enough that enemies can interrupt it — built-in combat vulnerability prevents abuse
Stunned 2 on disruption: meaningful punishment for having the cocoon destroyed; the target loses their rest AND loses actions — appropriate deterrent for fragile rest windows
Cannot be cast while there is an active combat threat: hard combat restriction enforced in the description
overridable: The 'no combat threat' restriction could be removed if the author prefers to allow the spell in dangerous situations (e.g., a protected chamber behind a locked door) — removing this makes the spell potentially abusable
The cocoon HP could be increased to 40 (Hardness 10) at base rank if the author feels 20 HP is too fragile for a rank-6 spell
checklistFailures: The 'time' trait is a custom homebrew trait. See Jolt note for series-wide flag.

Rest-compression spells have no precedent in PF2e Remaster. The converted version enforces a 'no active combat threat' restriction to prevent in-combat use, but this restriction is not a PF2e standard mechanic — it is a GM-enforced narrative constraint. Flagged for explicit table agreement.

Compression.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Gaseous Form (rank 4, primal, pass through cracks, resist physical) but Compression is rank 3 with more restrictions and willing only
Compression.archetype: utility/polymorph (2D form for movement and infiltration)
balanceBullets: Gaseous Form (rank 4) gives similar benefits (pass through gaps, resist physical damage) but the target can fly and take more actions. Compression at rank 3 is weaker: no flying, only Stride or revert, 1-minute reversion time.

Action restriction (only Stride or revert) is the primary cost that keeps this at rank 3 rather than rank 4. A 2D creature that can still attack, cast, and use skills would be stronger than Gaseous Form.
Resistance 5 to non-magical physical is below full resistance; appropriate for rank 3 as a partial protection.
Polymorph trait is correctly applied: this is a body-shape transformation. Does not stack with wild shape or other polymorphs.
8-hour duration (exploration tier) is appropriate for an infiltration/scouting utility that requires time to use, not a combat tool.
overridable: The action restriction (only Stride or revert) could relax at the GM's discretion for specific narrative uses — e.g., 'the 2D form can use social skills by speaking' — but full action access would make this too powerful at rank 3.
Resistance 5 to physical could extend to magical physical sources if the GM wants the spell to feel more 'complete' — currently only non-magical is covered at base.

Compressive Weapon.anchor: no clean analog — closest is True Strike (rank 1, +circumstance to hit) but this is a unique reach-extension effect
Compressive Weapon.archetype: utility/buff (melee reach extension via spatial compression)
balanceBullets: No PF2e analog for 'compress space to extend melee reach.' The 5e 'advantage on next two attacks' was repurposed because PF2e has no advantage mechanic.

Redesigned as a sustained reach-extension: target any creature within 30 ft with melee weapons. This is a genuinely unique tactical effect — casters can contribute melee Strikes at range without the spell being an attack itself.
Sustained duration (up to 1 min) is the appropriate tier for a concentration-requiring combat buff.

The rank-2 placement is justified by the utility: a permanent 30-ft melee range would let a caster always flank, never provoke AoO for retreating, and deny enemies the normal defensive advantage of range — that's above rank-1 budget.
overridable: Could be rebuilt to mirror the 5e original more closely: '+2 circumstance bonus to the next two attack rolls against a designated target' (closest PF2e equivalent to advantage on 2 attacks).
The 30-ft range cap (if target moves out, spell ends) could be softened to 'if target moves beyond 30 ft, make a DC 15 flat check to maintain.'

Cone of Decay.anchor: Desiccate (rank 8) — 10d10 void basic Fortitude, any number of living creatures; Cone of Decay is 1 rank lower, cone-shaped, with gear effects
balanceBullets: Desiccate at rank 8 deals 10d10 void on basic Fortitude. Cone of Decay at rank 7 deals 8d10 void on basic Fortitude — 1d10 below Desiccate at 1 rank lower, which is the correct +1d10/rank scaling for a single-target save spell.

Gear destruction (organic gear on failure, metal penalty on crit-fail) is the spell's distinctive feature; this creates a meaningful tactical effect beyond damage without being 'free' — it only triggers on failure/crit-fail.
Undead extra damage (4d10 void on crit-fail) is properly gated to the worst save tier — this is the Everything Spell check: the rider only appears on crit-fail (5–10% of outcomes).
Cone shape (60 ft) at rank 7 is within the canonical range table (60-ft cone at ranks 6–7).
Fortitude save is the correct organ-map for Con-save body-decay damage.
overridable: The gear-destruction effect could require a separate save or be limited to unattended gear — a GM may find destroying PC gear too punishing.
The metal-gear penalty could be removed to simplify the spell — the organic gear destruction alone is the signature effect.
Undead extra damage could be removed if the GM wants a pure-decay flavor without anti-undead niche.

Cone of Silence.anchor: Silence (rank 2 in 5e; PF2e has Silence as rank 2 utility) — Cone of Silence is the offensive/larger-area combat variant; a 60-ft cone affecting all creatures is rank 5 by the mass-effect scaling
balanceBullets: 60-foot cone (reduced from 5e's 90 feet) matches the rank-5 cone benchmark from SKILL.md (rank 5 = up to 60-ft cone); 90 ft is above-norm without a corresponding trade-off
Fortitude save for the silencing effect (not Will): deafness is a physical sensory deprivation (hearing organs), which is a Fortitude effect in PF2e — not a mental effect
Sustained up to 1 minute (5e concentration 10 min → 1 min): combat-grade control aura cap per plan
Cannot use auditory/linguistic spell traits while deafened inside cone is a meaningful combat trade-off for spellcaster enemies (prevents Linguistic and Auditory trait spell casting)
overridable: Fortitude save choice (not Will): the GM may prefer Will save for a 'stop the noise in your mind' interpretation; Fortitude was chosen because deafness is physical (ears), not mental

The cone following line of sight as the caster turns is faithful to the 5e text but creates tracking complexity at the table — GM may prefer a fixed-direction cone that must be re-aimed with a Sustain action

Connection.anchor: Sending (rank 5) — telepathic message any distance, 5% planar miss
balanceBullets: Anchored to Sending at rank 5: planetary range, mental, 5% planar miss preserved verbatim.

Key delta from Sending: durative two-way conversation (10 min) vs Sending's one-shot 25-word exchange. The duration tier and the multi-creature heightened upgrades are the entire reason this sits at rank 5 doing more than Sending.

Duration shortened from 5e's 1 hour to PF2e's 10-min exploration-utility tier (per plan rule: combat caps at 1 min/sustained, exploration steps at 10 min / 1 hr / 8 hr). Rank-8 heightened restores the 1 hour.
Material cost converted from 5e 500 gp to PF2e 50 gp pearl — PF2e gp economy is roughly 10× cheaper than 5e at the same tier; matches the Talisman / focus-component economy.
Subtle trait added: matches Sending; no visible sign once the 1-min cast completes.
overridable: If you want it to be a true upgrade over Sending, drop the planar miss chance entirely instead of preserving 5%.
Could be made a ritual (1 hour to cast, no slot) — the 1-minute cast already pushes it toward ritual feel.
Heightened (7th/8th/9th) cadence could compress to a single Heightened (+2) granting +2 targets and +1 duration tier.

Containment Orbs.anchor: Spell Turning (5e rank 7) — spell reflection; PF2e closest is Dispel Magic + readied reaction, but Containment Orbs adds an explosive payoff
balanceBullets: The detonation damage (3d6 per absorbed spell rank) is the payoff: absorbing a rank-7 enemy spell and detonating deals 21d6 (~73 avg) to a 20-foot burst — this matches Fireball at rank 9–10, but requires the orb to successfully absorb a high-rank spell first, which is a conditional benefit.
Three orbs create up to three opportunities to absorb and detonate — but each orb is specific to one tradition, so players must predict enemy spell types.
Sustained up to 10 minutes is exploration-tier — appropriate since the spell is a reactive defense, not an active attack.
The 2-action detonation cost prevents zero-action-economy payoffs.
Force damage on detonation is thematically appropriate (magical energy released) and rarely resisted.
overridable: Detonation damage multiplier (3d6 per rank) could be reduced to 2d6 per rank if the potential maximum feels too swingy (absorbing a rank-10 spell would deal 30d6 ≈ 105 avg at 3d6/rank).
Tradition assignment (arcane/divine/occult/primal) could be replaced with school of magic if the GM prefers the 5e school system.
Could limit detonation range to 'within 30 feet' rather than 'within 20 feet of you' to prevent the caster from retreating to safety.

Copy.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Illusory Writing (rank 1) for interacting with written text
balanceBullets: No direct PF2e analog; closest is Illusory Writing (rank 1) which interacts with written text. Copy is purely practical (not illusion-based) and operates instantaneously.
Rank 1 is appropriate: this is a scribal utility with no combat use. The 50-page limit, magical-writing caveat, and Recall Knowledge detection check are the three safety valves.
1-minute cast time is preserved as the rate-limiting factor preventing 'instant duplicate any document in one action.'
Mundane text — no combat value. Magical-writing copy — useful but non-magical copy doesn't let you cast spells from a copied spellbook, which is the most powerful potential abuse.
overridable: The Recall Knowledge detection check could be removed if the GM wants the copy to be truly perfect (no detection).
Could be made rank 0 (cantrip) if limited to 1 page per cast, for a truly minor utility effect.

Darkseeker's Aura.anchor: Wall of Fire (rank 4, 4d6 fire per crossing) — Darkseeker's Aura provides a weaker passive aura (2d6 on-hit) plus a one-shot heavy attack, sustained 1 min
balanceBullets: 2d6 acid retaliation per melee hit is weaker than Wall of Fire's 4d6 but applies to any melee attacker (not just crossing a wall) — the triggering condition is more frequent, hence lower damage per trigger.
Resistance 10 to acid is appropriate for rank 4 (Resist Energy heightened to rank 4 gives resistance 10).
8d6 focused attack (28 avg) is roughly the rank-4 High column for a melee spell attack — justified because it expends the entire aura.
Sustained 1 minute (not 1 hour as in 5e): combat-grade buffs cap at 1 min per plan rules.
overridable: The retaliation damage could be reduced to 1d6 if the passive-trigger frequency (any melee hit) is deemed too punishing for martial-heavy encounters.
Acid resistance could be replaced with a general damage resistance to a chosen energy type (chosen at cast) for broader applicability.
checklistFailures: Checklist item 7 — Duration: 5e had concentration 1 hour; PF2e caps combat-grade buffs at 1 minute sustained. Deliberate downgrade per plan rules.

Darkseeker's Restraint.anchor: Slither (rank 5: 3d6 piercing + 1d6 persistent poison, Reflex save, grabbed on fail, restrained on crit fail) — Darkseeker's Restraint is the Will-save variant with higher damage and a sustained single-target focus rather than a burst AoE
balanceBullets: Incapacitation trait mandatory: restrained (grabbed + immobilized) on a failed Will save means the creature cannot move, which effectively removes it from the fight as a mobile combatant — this meets the incapacitation threshold per conditions.md

Damage: failure tier = 3d8 (avg 13.5) initial + 3d8 per turn; crit fail = 6d8 (avg 27) initial + 6d8 per turn. This is below Slither's persistent-damage pattern but appropriate for a single-target sustained Will-save spell
Will save (5e Wisdom save → PF2e Will) correct: the chains bind through force of will/spirit; stygian chains are a psychic/planar coercion effect
Sustained duration (must spend 1 action/round) creates action economy cost for the caster; the chains do not persist for free
overridable: The damage split between grabbed (failure) and restrained (crit fail) is a design interpretation: 5e only described 'restrained' as the main outcome with 6d8 both initial and per-turn; in PF2e, grabbed is the baseline fail and restrained is the escalated crit-fail — the 5e damage values are split across these tiers accordingly

Will save vs. Reflex save: Slither uses Reflex (dodge the tentacles); Darkseeker's uses Will (resist the stygian binding). This is a deliberate differentiation; GM may prefer Reflex for physical chains

Dead Ringer.anchor: Invisibility heightened to 4th (rank 4, 1 min, hostile-immune) — Dead Ringer adds the illusory-corpse component and uses a reaction trigger, placing it at rank 4 but with a more restrictive trigger
balanceBullets: Reaction trigger (succeed on a save or be missed) is a strong but fair condition — it requires the enemy to have just failed to harm you, so it is situationally rather than universally applicable.
Invisibility ending on attack/spell is the standard rule — no special exception granted, keeping this in line with Invisibility's balance.
The illusory corpse duplicate is primarily a narrative/social tool (convincing enemies you're dead) rather than a combat power multiplier.
Sustained up to 1 hour is acceptable: the invisibility ends on any attack/spell, so the hour-long duration only matters for extended stealth sequences, not combat.
overridable: The trigger could be restricted to 'missed by a melee attack' only (removing the 'succeed on a saving throw' trigger) to tighten the reaction window.
Could add a Stealth bonus while invisible in addition to the undetected condition.

Deja Vu.anchor: no clean analog — closest is Retributive Pain (rank 2, divine/occult reaction) for reaction-damage pattern
balanceBullets: Anchored loosely to Retributive Pain (rank 2): a reaction that deals damage to a creature that just hurt an ally. This spell does similar but punishes any targeted attack or save.

Mental damage up to 4d6 (rank-2 single-target moderate strike is ~14 avg; 4d6 avg 14 matches). The 'up to' clause means it only matches the triggering damage, preventing exploitation against low-damage sources.
Will save (Wis→Will) is the correct organ for time-echo mental trauma. Non-basic save.
The save re-roll rider (only applies when trigger was a succeeded save) is the spell's elegant second function — it can turn an enemy's save success into a second bite of the apple.
overridable: The save re-roll could be made a separate heightened effect (base: just mental damage; rank 4: adds save retry) to simplify the base version.
The damage cap could be removed (always 4d6 regardless of triggering damage) for simpler play, making it a standard reaction-damage spell.

Disperse Magic.anchor: Counterspell (rank varies) — magical defense reaction; closer to a personal Shield-equivalent vs spells
Disperse Magic.archetype: reaction-defense (magic absorption, personal saving throw boost)
balanceBullets: +2 circumstance bonus to a save as a reaction is slightly stronger than the rank-1 Resist Spell tradition cantrips but justified at rank 2 by the 'better damage tier on success' rider.
The damage improvement (success = no damage instead of half) is the primary value; this turns every basic-save damage spell into a 'succeed = no damage' situation, which is the 5e 'evasion' fantasy.
1-action reaction cast (reaction in PF2e) is appropriate: this is a defensive response, not an offensive action.
No tradition restriction on the triggering effect — it works against any spell or magical effect, which is consistent with an abjuration 'disperse the magic' feel.
overridable: The +2 circumstance bonus could be replaced with 'roll the save twice, take the better result' (fortune effect) which more closely mirrors 5e's advantage — but fortune stacking rules make this riskier.
Could be restricted to only spells (not magical effects) for tighter balance.

Disrupt Movement.anchor: Slow (rank 3, single target) — Speed reduction + action debuff; adapted to rank 1 multi-target with sustained duration
balanceBullets: Anchored to Slow at rank 3 (single target, slowed 1 = speed halved + 1 action lost); Disrupt Movement does only Speed-halved (no action loss) across up to 3 targets at rank 1.
Speed reduction without action loss is a Tier B debuff — appropriate at rank 1 with sustained duration and end-of-turn saves.
Three-target spread at rank 1 is offset by: (a) sustained requirement, (b) each target gets an end-of-turn save, (c) Reflex save (not Will/Fort, which enemies tend to be weaker at).
Heightened 3rd adds immobilized on crit fail only, scaling toward Slow's level of control without reaching it.
overridable: Save could be changed to Will (Wis→Will) since spatial confusion might be more mental; Fortitude would also work as a bodily resistance to spatial compression.
Could target only 1 creature at rank 1 for tighter balance, and heighten to 3 targets at rank 3.

Distorted Mark.anchor: Live Wire (cantrip) — dual-damage auto-hit rider on hit; crit +persistent; +1d4 per +2 ranks
balanceBullets: Anchored to Live Wire cantrip: hybrid attack+spell mechanic where the weapon Strike is the delivery vehicle and the spell delivers a triggered rider.

Decompression damage is 1d4 sonic (unconditional auto-trigger, no save) — this is below the cantrip floor but justified because it stacks on top of a weapon Strike that already deals full weapon damage.
Heightening at +1d4 per +2 ranks (loaded-cantrip cadence) rather than +1d4 per +1 rank, because the auto-trigger decompression bypasses saves entirely — that warrants the slower cadence.
5e caster-modifier rider dropped entirely (cantrips in PF2e do not scale off ability scores); flat 1d4 replaced it.
overridable: Could be redesigned as a 1-action 'touch' cantrip rather than requiring a melee weapon Strike, making it more broadly accessible to non-martial casters.
The sonic damage type could be changed to force (fits the 'space decompresses' fiction equally well, and force is rarely resisted).
Heightening cadence could be changed to +1d4 per +1 rank (standard cantrip) if the GM feels the auto-trigger nature is acceptable at standard speed.

Divine Regression.anchor: Spiritual Weapon / Vampiric Feast (rank 3) — melee spell attack + ongoing void effect; scaled down to rank 2
balanceBullets: Anchored loosely to rank-3 Vampiric Feast (6d6 void, basic Fortitude, touch) as the nearest void-damage melee spell. Scaled down to rank 2: 4d8 void (~18) at the rank-2 high spell-attack column (~2d10+4 = 15).

Heal-reversal is the spell's unique mechanical identity; it turns enemy healing into additional void damage, which is a powerful effect. This justifies the damage sitting slightly above the rank-2 moderate benchmark.
Fortitude save at end of each turn is the recovery mechanism; this prevents the spell from being a permanent debuff while also giving the target agency.
Named as Divine Regression but works via a void melee attack — traditions set to divine + occult to match void/necrotic's spirit+life (divine) and mind+spirit (occult) essence.
overridable: Could be reduced to 3d8 void to sit cleanly at the rank-2 moderate benchmark, then heightened +1d8/+1.
The heal-reversal could be limited to only magical healing (not fast healing/regeneration) for a less punishing version.

Djura's Divine Protection.anchor: Energy Aegis (rank 7, resistance 5 to all 8 energy types) — mass physical resistance at rank 9 calibrated above Energy Aegis by 2 ranks = resistance 10
balanceBullets: Resistance 10 to B/P/S and force for 8 targets at rank 9 — Energy Aegis (rank 7) gives resistance 5 to all 8 energy types for 1 creature; scaling up 2 ranks doubles the resistance and extends to 8 targets, which is calibrated at rank 9

+2 status to dying flat checks (DC 11 → effectively DC 9) is a meaningful death-protection buff without being unkillable; 5e advantage is roughly a +5 effective bonus which would be too strong, so +2 status is the conservative conversion
10-minute exploration-grade duration is appropriate for pre-combat warding; does not need to be sustained because it is a passive resistance layer
8 targets at 30-ft range at rank 9: Haste heightened to rank 7 hits 6 targets; rank 9 for 8 targets is proportional
overridable: Resistance value: 5e was full resistance (half damage) which is effectively resistance equal to half incoming damage — a flat resistance 10 is more PF2e-idiomatic and avoids the 'scales with hit power' issue; GM may use resistance 15 to be closer to 5e feel

Named focus-spell suggestion: Djura's Divine Protection fits the PF2e focus-spell template (class-specific, strong effect, single cast per recharge) — GM may convert to a focus spell for a Djura paladin archetype

Djura's Divine Razor.anchor: Wall of Fire (rank 4, sustained damage rider) — adapted as a 1-action self-buff with a per-hit curse
balanceBullets: 1-action rank-5 slot is strictly weaker than 2-action; justified because the effect is a self-melee-rider, not a damage spell in its own right
3d10 initial bonus (avg 16.5 force) + 2d6 per-hit curse (avg 7 force) lands in the 'strong crit-hit rider' range for rank 5 — similar power to Polar Ray's drained 2 rider but self-melee-gated
Force damage type pricing 0.80× means nominal dice are slightly generous; acceptable because it's a class-flavor spell with a melee weapon restriction
Per-turn Will save to remove the curse gives the target meaningful agency; the curse typically lasts ~3 rounds before the target breaks free, giving the caster 2–3 bonus hits
overridable: The per-turn Will save to remove the curse could instead be 'end of turn after taking damage from the curse' to make it more dramatic
Focus spell suggestion: Djura's Divine Razor fits the pattern of a Champion or Cleric divine weapon-enhancement focus spell perfectly; flag for the author

Djura's Righteous Pressure.anchor: Spirit Song (rank 4, occult, 20-ft emanation that deals spirit damage to undead) — Djura's is divine-only, 30-ft radius, with forced expulsion rather than pure damage
balanceBullets: Named-caster spell (Djura's) flagged — PF2e-idiomatic form would be a champion reaction or focus spell; kept as slotted spell per plan rules.
2d6 vitality damage per round only harms undead (vitality is harmless to fiends unless they have undead-type vulnerability). The forced-expulsion on failure is the primary anti-fiend mechanism.
Holy trait is correct: this is explicitly an anti-fiend/anti-undead divine aura.
Fortitude save (Con organ mapping from 5e Con save) is correct for a physical-body-based expulsion.
overridable: The vitality damage could be changed to spirit damage (which bypasses incorporeality and affects both undead and fiends equally) for a more unified anti-supernatural effect.
The 'cannot reenter until next turn' clause could be tightened to 'must succeed on a new Fortitude save to reenter' to allow persistent reentry attempts.
checklistFailures: Checklist item 6 — vitality damage only harms undead (not fiends) under PF2e rules. The anti-fiend component relies entirely on the expulsion effect. Logged as a deviation from 5e's 'radiant damages both' design intent. Overridable: change to spirit damage or holy damage to affect both equally.

Do My Bidding.anchor: Dominate (rank 6) — incapacitation Will save, full control of one creature; Do My Bidding is mass-charm (not full control) at rank 7
balanceBullets: Dominate at rank 6 fully controls one creature on a failed Will save. Do My Bidding at rank 7 partially compels a crowd toward a goal with a Will save — less total control (goal-constrained, self-led), mass application.
Incapacitation trait is mandatory: creatures under the effect are compelled to pursue dangerous goals, which is removal from autonomous decision-making.
10-minute cast time is the primary balance lever — this cannot be used mid-combat and requires significant setup investment.
8-hour duration is exploration-tier; not combat-grade.
Will save (Wis→Will organ-map for mental enchantment) is correct; auditory and linguistic traits properly gate deaf/language-barrier creatures.
overridable: Duration could be reduced to 1 hour at base with heightening to 8 hours at rank 9 for cleaner progression.
Could add uncommon rarity — mass crowd compulsion has significant social and political setting implications.
The 'does not realize it was charmed' clause could be removed if the GM wants to preserve story tension of PC revelation.

Earworm.anchor: Scrying (rank 6, divine/occult, 1 min, see/hear through sensor at any range); Earworm is rank 3, 8 hours, but requires touch, no visual at base, and Fort save
balanceBullets: Scrying (rank 6) gives both sight and sound at any range; Earworm (rank 3) is touch-range implant, audio only at base, 8 hours. The touch requirement and single-sense limitation justify 3 ranks below Scrying.
Fortitude save is correct: a physical worm being implanted into body tissue is a physical intrusion resisted by the body's constitution, not the mind.
8-hour duration is exploration-tier appropriate; the target is unaware, making this a surveillance asset rather than a combat tool.
Crit-fail visual eavesdropping is the power-escalation tier — seeing through the target's eyes is Scrying-adjacent and appropriately gated to crit fail only.
Auditory trait gates this against deaf creatures and deaf-immune monsters, which is thematically correct (no ears → no earworm).
overridable: Could add a Perception check for the target each day to feel the arcane thread (currently only a Seek action by the target) — stricter if the GM wants the spell to have higher counterplay.
The range to implant could increase to 10 feet at base (gentle somatic gesture) rather than touch, if the GM finds the touch requirement too restrictive for a spy spell.

Ebb and Flow.anchor: Haste (rank 3, +1 action, 1 min) + Slow (rank 3, slowed 1 on fail, 1 min); Ebb and Flow does both simultaneously in an AoE
balanceBullets: Haste + Slow at rank 3 combined into a single AoE zone is the 'Everything Spell' risk. Mitigated by: (a) ally buff is weaker than full Haste (+10 Speed + extra reaction vs +1 full action), (b) enemy debuff requires a Will save, (c) 20-ft burst only, (d) sustained.

Will save for enemies is correct (temporal/mental perception of time). Slowed 1 + action limit on fail is weaker than Slow's full effect (Slow can give slowed 2 on crit fail with no anti-multi-attack); the no-multi-Strike clause compensates.
The 20-foot burst at 60 feet is within rank-3 AoE norms (benchmark shows 20-ft burst at rank 3).
Sustained up to 1 minute is the correct combat cap for a dual buff/debuff aura — Haste and Slow are both 1 minute sustained; this matches.
The 'time' trait is a custom trait flagged as potentially non-immunitable; the spell's effects are still gated by the mental trait on saves.
overridable: Could remove the allied extra-reaction benefit to reduce the spell's dual-axis power, keeping only the movement bonus — this would make the enemy-debuff axis clearly the primary function.
The 'no multi-Strike' anti-flurry clause could be replaced with a simpler slowed 1 (matching Slow) if the GM prefers standard conditions over custom action restrictions.
checklistFailures: Design tension: Combining Haste-level ally buff with Slow-level enemy debuff in a single AoE at rank 3 risks the 'Everything Spell' anti-pattern. Mitigations applied (weaker-than-Haste ally buff, Will save required for enemies, 20-ft burst only, sustained). Flagged for GM review — could reasonably be rank 4 if the combined effect proves too strong at table.

Eldrich Horror.anchor: Quandary (rank 8, incapacitation, extradimensional removal) + Slither (rank 5, tentacle grab) — rank 9 combining both patterns at larger scale
Eldrich Horror.archetype: area control + incapacitation — Far Realms portal with tendrils
balanceBullets: 3-action cast justified: portal + 4 tendrils + ongoing damage inside Far Realms is a very complex effect; 2-action would feel under-costed for a rank-9 multi-element spell with sustained maintenance
incapacitation MANDATORY: creatures pulled into the Far Realms portal are extradimensionally removed from combat — this is the definitive incapacitation scenario

4d6–8d6 void per round (save-dependent) inside the portal is calibrated below rank-9 standalone damage (Massacre: 9d6 / 100 / death) because the portal already has the combat-removal component plus the HP-maximum reduction rider

HP maximum reduction on failure mirrors the 5e 'max HP reduced by same amount' mechanic — this is a void damage side effect (void damage can reduce max HP) which fits the Far Realms corruption fiction
overridable: 4 tendrils: 5e gave the caster full control of all 4 targets each round; PF2e version matches — GM may limit to 1 tendril attack per round to reduce complexity

Portal entry: 5e had a Dex save to leap out when the portal opens; PF2e Reflex save matches — GM may make this a free action rather than a save if they want creatures to more easily escape the initial manifestation

Elemental Sink.anchor: Hex Cantrip (occult) — sustained single-target damage rider; closest published analog is persistent small-damage riders on Witch hexes
balanceBullets: No perfect PF2e anchor; closest is the Witch's Cackle/Hex sustained damage pattern. The 1d4 additional damage per hit is intentionally low (below rank-1 Wall of Fire per-round output of 4d6) because it applies to every incoming Strike, not just once per round.

Reduced from 5e's 1d6 to 1d4 because: (a) rank-1 per-hit riders are most comparable to a Hex, which sits at 1d4; (b) 1d6 per-hit sustained at rank 1 would exceed the rank-1 limited-use area damage on rounds 2-3.
